intro: Birmingham rewards visitors with a walkable centre, rich industrial heritage and lively food and nightlife. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: West Midlands Metro trams link the centre with Wolverhampton and Edgbaston; fares are a few pounds.
Buses are frequent and run by National Express West Midlands; a Daysaver day ticket costs about £4-5.
Taxis are metered; Uber and Bolt both operate in the city.
Driving is easy on motorways but the centre is congested and parking is costly.
The centre is compact and mostly pedestrianised, so walking is best for short trips.
Cycling is possible but cycle lanes are few; canal towpaths make pleasant routes.

peaky-blinders.name: Peaky Blinders trail and locations
peaky-blinders.price_text: Self-guided walk free · guided tours vary, check on the day
peaky-blinders.hours: Outdoor locations always visible · guided tours run on set days
peaky-blinders.tip: The show is set in 1920s Birmingham but filmed mostly elsewhere. Start at the real locations in the city centre and Digbeth.

villa-park.name: Villa Park stadium tour
villa-park.price_text: Tour prices vary, check on the day
villa-park.hours: Tours on selected days, not matchdays · check on the day
villa-park.tip: Book ahead and avoid matchdays. The ground is a short train ride from the city centre.

university-birmingham.name: University of Birmingham and Old Joe clock tower
university-birmingham.hours: Campus open daily · buildings have their own hours
university-birmingham.tip: Old Joe is one of the tallest freestanding clock towers in the world. The campus is green and easy to walk.

university-warwick.name: University of Warwick campus
university-warwick.tip: This is outside the city, near Coventry. Allow travel time and check trains or buses on the day.

chesters.name: Chester's
chesters.price_text: Prices vary, check on the day
chesters.tip: Confirm the address and opening hours before you go, as details can change.

bullring-market.name: Bullring and Bullring Markets
bullring-market.price_text: Free to enter · food priced per stall
bullring-market.hours: Market days vary · shops roughly 09:00–20:00, check on the day
bullring-market.tip: The indoor market is good for cheap, fresh food. The Bull statue outside is the classic photo stop.

library-viewpoint.name: Library of Birmingham secret garden viewpoint
library-viewpoint.hours: Library hours vary, check on the day
library-viewpoint.tip: Go up to the upper terraces for a free view over the city. It is a good short stop.

canal-walk.name: Brindleyplace and canal walk
canal-walk.tip: Birmingham has more canals than Venice, so walk a stretch at dusk. Bars and restaurants line the water.

jewellery-quarter-walk.name: Jewellery Quarter walk
jewellery-quarter-walk.price_text: Free · museum entry may charge, check on the day
jewellery-quarter-walk.hours: Streets always open · shops and museum have own hours
jewellery-quarter-walk.tip: Look for the old workshops and small jewellers. It is quieter than the centre and good for a slow wander.

digbeth-street-art.name: Digbeth street art and creative quarter
digbeth-street-art.tip: Wander the side streets for murals and independent venues. Some areas feel rough at night, so go by day.

balti-tour.name: Balti triangle food tour
balti-tour.price_text: Meal prices vary, check on the day
balti-tour.tip: Birmingham is the home of the balti. Book a table or a guided food tour in advance.

cadbury-world.name: Cadbury World
cadbury-world.price_text: Ticket prices vary, book online, check on the day
cadbury-world.hours: Usually daytime, closed some weekdays · check on the day
cadbury-world.tip: Book online in advance. It is south of the city and best reached by train.

thinktank.name: Thinktank Science Museum
thinktank.price_text: Ticket prices vary, check on the day
thinktank.tip: Good for families and rainy days. It sits in the Millennium Point building in the east of the centre.

gas-street-basin.name: Gas Street Basin
gas-street-basin.tip: The meeting point of two canal systems. Sit by the water with a drink and watch the narrowboats.

st-philips.name: St Philip's Cathedral and square
st-philips.tip: A quiet green square in the busy centre. Look for the Burne-Jones stained glass inside.

mailbox.name: The Mailbox and canal-side bars
mailbox.hours: Venues open into the evening, check on the day
mailbox.tip: Good for an evening drink by the water. Combine it with the nearby canal walk.

selfridges.name: Bullring shopping and Selfridges building
selfridges.tip: The curved silver building is a city icon. Shop here on a rainy afternoon.

hippodrome.name: Birmingham Hippodrome show
hippodrome.price_text: Ticket prices vary by show, book ahead
hippodrome.tip: Book ahead for big shows. It is next to the Arcadian in the Chinese Quarter.

cannon-hill-park.name: Cannon Hill Park
cannon-hill-park.tip: A large green park south of the centre. Good for a picnic or a walk after the university.

coffin-works.name: Coffin Works museum
coffin-works.price_text: Ticket prices vary, check on the day
coffin-works.hours: Selected days, check on the day
coffin-works.tip: A small, unusual museum in the Jewellery Quarter. Check opening days before you travel.

brindleyplace-food.name: Brindleyplace restaurants
brindleyplace-food.hours: Lunch and dinner, check on the day
brindleyplace-food.tip: Plenty of choice by the canals. Book ahead on weekends.

grand-central.name: Grand Central and New Street
grand-central.tip: A handy stop for shopping and trains. Use it as a base to reach other areas.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Industrial heritage, canals and the old workshops.

stays.why: Walk to New Street station, the Bullring and the museums. Best base for a first visit.
Canalside bars and restaurants, close to the ICC and the Sea Life centre. Quiet at night.
Historic workshops, small museums and good cafés. A short tram or walk from the centre.
Creative quarter with street art, venues and the coach station. Livelier and cheaper.

food: Try a balti curry: the dish is linked to Birmingham. Expect around £10–15 for a main in the Balti Triangle.
Digbeth and the city centre have street-food markets and food halls; check opening days on the day.
The Jewellery Quarter has independent cafés and bakeries; good for a cheap lunch.
Brindleyplace and the canalside are best for sit-down dinners; book ahead at weekends.
A pint in a traditional pub is a local ritual; prices vary, so check the board.
more_time: Swap a city afternoon for a canal walk or narrowboat trip; the towpaths are flat and free.
Take a short train ride to Stratford-upon-Avon or Warwick for Shakespeare and castle history; check times and fares on the day.
Add a day for the Black Country Living Museum if industrial history interests you; check opening days first.
